tools.name: api_status
tools.description: Check the Elfa API key tier, credit usage and remaining requests, and confirm the API is reachable. Free. Call this first when a request fails with an auth or credit error. historyFrom is the earliest time, in unix seconds, the events, market and calls tools read on this plan.

tools.name: mentions
tools.description: Social mentions from X and Telegram. 1 credit per call. Returns engagement metrics and a link per post, not the post text. mode=top ranks one ticker's mentions by engagement. mode=search filters by keywords or by account. mode=news returns the token news feed, which is X posts from accounts tagged as news sources rather than articles from news outlets.

mode.description: top needs ticker. search needs keywords or accountName. news is a feed and needs neither.

ticker.description: Ticker for mode=top, for example "BTC" or "$SOL".

keywords.description: Up to 5 comma separated keywords for mode=search.

accountName.description: X username for mode=search, without the @.

coinIds.description: Comma separated CoinGecko coin ids to filter mode=news.

searchType.description: How multiple keywords combine in mode=search.

from.description: Start of an absolute range, unix seconds. Use with to. For mode=search the range must span at least 1 day and at most 30.

to.description: End of an absolute range, unix seconds. Use with from.

pageSize.description: Items per page, up to 100. Keep it small and page through rather than asking for everything at once.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous mode=search response.

verbosity.description: concise returns the high signal fields only. Use detailed when you need every metric.

tools.name: trending
tools.description: What is gaining social attention right now. 1 credit per call. scope=tokens returns tickers ranked by mention volume with the change against the previous window. scope=contracts_twitter and scope=contracts_telegram return trending contract addresses.

timeWindow.description: Relative window such as "24h" or "7d". Defaults to 24h unless both from and to are given.

from.description: Start of an absolute range, unix seconds. Use with to.

to.description: End of an absolute range, unix seconds. Use with from.

pageSize.description: Items per page, up to 100. Keep it small and page through rather than asking for everything at once.

minMentions.description: Drop entries below this mention count.

tools.name: narratives
tools.description: Written narrative analysis with source links, for when counts are not enough. 5 credits per call, so prefer trending or mentions when metrics will do. scope=market extracts the narratives moving the market. scope=keywords summarises events for keywords you supply, and can take over a minute to return.

scope.description: market is a broad sweep. keywords needs the keywords argument.

keywords.description: Up to 5 comma separated keywords for scope=keywords.

searchType.description: How multiple keywords combine for scope=keywords.

maxNarratives.description: Cap the narratives returned for scope=market.

maxTweetsPerNarrative.description: Cap the sources per narrative for scope=market.

from.description: Start of an absolute range, unix seconds. Use with to.

to.description: End of an absolute range, unix seconds. Use with from.

tools.name: account_stats
tools.description: Smart follower and engagement stats for an X account. 1 credit per call. Use it to judge whether an account's reach is real before weighting what it posts. Returns raw metrics, not a reputation score, so the signal is in the ratios. Legacy: it still works today and keeps working until 28 October 2026, when it will be removed, and it is not being extended before then. Build new work on mentions with mode=search, which returns the posting account alongside each post's engagement metrics.

username.description: X username, with or without the @.

tools.name: market_chat
tools.description: Ask Elfa for written market analysis grounded in its social data. Costs credits and varies by speed, so fast is the cheaper option. Pass sessionId from a previous reply to continue the same conversation. The reply includes sources: links to the posts and pages the research read (links only, not their text), so you can cite or check them.

analysisType.description: chat needs message. tokenIntro and tokenAnalysis need symbol, or chain plus contractAddress. accountAnalysis needs username. macro and summary need nothing else.

speed.description: Defaults to fast, which is cheaper and shallower. Ask for expert when the answer needs deeper reasoning.

tools.name: auto_build
tools.description: Turn a plain-language monitoring request into an EQL query. Costs 1 credit plus LLM usage. This only drafts the query, nothing starts running until you activate it with auto_query_write. Say what to watch, the threshold, and what should happen when it fires. It drafts tweet conditions only for accounts in Elfa's real-time set (included); for any other X account, write the condition yourself and check it with auto_validate.

message.description: What to monitor, in plain language, for example "tell me on Telegram when BTC funding on Binance goes negative".

speed.description: fast is cheaper, expert reasons more deeply about the query.

sessionId.description: Continue refining a query from an earlier reply.

tools.name: auto_validate
tools.description: Check EQL syntax and get a cost estimate before anything is activated. Free. Always run this before auto_query_write, and show the estimated cost to the user. tweetAccounts lists the X account behind each tweet condition: billing=per_post accounts cost creditsPerPost for every post from the account (not replies or reposts), matched or not, while the query runs, on top of estimatedCredits, so state that too. Pass either an inline query or a draftId. method=symbol instead checks that a symbol has market data on a venue, before you build price or ta conditions around it.

method.description: query validates EQL, symbol checks symbol support.

query.description: EQL query object with conditions, actions and expiresIn. Build it with auto_build and check it with auto_validate first. Use notify or webhook actions: a query carrying a credential, such as a telegram_bot botToken or a webhook signingSecret, is refused.

draftId.description: Validate a stored draft instead of an inline query.

title.description: Title to validate with the query.

description.description: Description to validate with the query.

tools.name: auto_query
tools.description: Read side of Auto. Free. method=list browses queries, method=get polls one query and returns its latest evaluation, plus failure when it failed with a recorded reason, method=executions and method=execution show what fired, method=sessions and method=session return the LLM analysis attached to a query. There is no push channel here, poll with method=get and respect pollAfterSeconds.

queryId.description: Required for get, sessions and session.

limit.description: Page size for list style methods.

tools.name: auto_query_write
tools.description: Activate, cancel or delete an Auto query. Creating costs 5 credits plus LLM usage, cancel and delete are free. An activated query runs unattended and fires its action without asking again, so validate it with auto_validate and confirm the cost, including any per-post X accounts, and the action with the user before calling this.

method.description: create activates a new query. cancel stops an active one. delete removes one that has already finished.

query.description: EQL query object with conditions, actions and expiresIn. Build it with auto_build and check it with auto_validate first. Use notify or webhook actions: a query carrying a credential, such as a telegram_bot botToken or a webhook signingSecret, is refused.

title.description: Short title shown in the notification when this fires.

description.description: Why this was set up, shown alongside the title.

tools.name: auto_draft
tools.description: Park an Auto query without activating it. Drafts never evaluate and never fire. Free, except method=convert which activates the draft and costs the same as creating a query. Use drafts when the user is still deciding.

method.description: upsert creates or updates a draft. convert activates it as a live query.

draftId.description: Required for get, delete and convert. Optional on upsert to update.

query.description: EQL query object with conditions, actions and expiresIn. Build it with auto_build and check it with auto_validate first. Use notify or webhook actions: a query carrying a credential, such as a telegram_bot botToken or a webhook signingSecret, is refused.

title.description: Title carried into the live query.

description.description: Description carried into the live query.

tools.name: entities
tools.description: Turn a ticker, $cashtag, name, @handle, contract address, CoinGecko id, FIGI or CIK into the entity id that events and calls take.. It matches exactly, it is not a search: a prefix or a misspelling returns nothing. A ticker is not unique, so take the first row and check its name, or narrow with entityType. Forms of an asset share one family id where known: WBTC and cbBTC are Bitcoin. Resolve once and reuse the id.

q.description: What you hold, for example "btc", "$SOL", "@VitalikButerin" or a contract address.

entityType.description: Narrow the match to these kinds. Omit to match every kind.

limit.description: Items per page, up to 200. Keep it small and page with cursor rather than asking for everything at once.

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous reply. Change any argument but limit and it fails; start again without it.

tools.name: events
tools.description: What is happening in crypto and equity markets, written up from posts across many sources.. level=events: what happened, what it names, how prices reacted where measured (impacts is empty on most events), and the posts behind it. level=storylines: the events of one development, threaded over days. level=arcs: storylines grouped into a larger movement. Search any level by topic with q, filter by asset with entityIds from the entities tool, or fetch up to 30 you hold with ids. Not returned: post text, a sentiment score or a price.

q.description: Search by topic, best match first, for example "stablecoin regulation". from becomes optional.

from.description: level=events or storylines. Start of the range, unix seconds, not milliseconds. Required unless you fetch by ids or search with q. Arcs take no from. api_status returns historyFrom, the earliest time your plan reads.

to.description: level=events or storylines. End of the range, unix seconds. Defaults to now.

ids.description: Fetch up to 30 you already hold, by id. No from needed.

entityIds.description: Up to 30 ids from the entities tool. Matches any of them.

eventClass.description: level=events. market: a development reported across posts. asset: posts about one asset. call: accounts taking positions.

eventType.description: level=events. What kind of development it is.

implication.description: level=events. Which way it cuts for the assets it names.

assetClass.description: level=events: events tied to this market by what they name, plus events tied to neither, such as macro news; a repeated query can return fewer as names get linked to assets. level=arcs: arcs with at least 15% of their events naming an asset in this market, then macro arcs.

novelty.description: level=events. update: a later reading of a story already served.

alertAction.description: level=events. alert: judged impactful. monitor: worth watching.

hasStoryline.description: level=events. true keeps events in a storyline, false those in none.

notable.description: level=events. true drops events their storyline marked as not material.

arcId.description: level=events. Events in one arc's storylines.

relation.description: level=storylines. Storylines holding an event of this relation.

status.description: level=storylines: open (default; every status with q), dormant or any. level=arcs: active (default) or retired.

sort.description: level=events: latest (default), or relevant, which ranks the last 24 hours and takes no from. level=arcs: latest, storylines or events.

limit.description: Items per page, up to 30. Keep it small and page with cursor rather than asking for everything at once.

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous reply. Change any argument but limit and it fails; start again without it.

tools.name: market
tools.description: Whole-market views, no asset needed.. view=mindshare ranks assets by share of attention over a period, with hot on those heating up. view=call_book is the crowd's long/short lean, one bar per hour plus a live tick: read crowdingPercentile rather than longShare, since the accounts lean long almost always. view=trending_contracts ranks contract addresses by how many posts pasted them, crypto only, and the unnamed ones are often the ones worth watching.

market.description: crypto or equity. trending_contracts is crypto only.

period.description: view=mindshare. The stretch share covers, ending at to. Default 4h.

from.description: view=call_book and view=trending_contracts, required. Start of the range, unix seconds, not milliseconds. Trending contracts read 30 days at most.

to.description: End of the range, unix seconds. Defaults to now.

minMentions.description: view=trending_contracts. Leave out addresses pasted fewer times. Default 5.

limit.description: Items per page, up to 200. Keep it small and page with cursor rather than asking for everything at once.

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous reply. Change any argument but limit and it fails; start again without it.

tools.name: calls
tools.description: What accounts are doing: positions taken in posts on X and Telegram.. level=calls: each post that opened, added to, trimmed, reaffirmed, reversed, closed or stopped out of a position. level=episodes: each position from open to close, with entry and exit prices and the author's track record. level=positioning: open longs and shorts on one asset right now. level=episodes with status=open and from set to now reads what every matching account holds right now. Not returned: post text or a recommendation.

entityId.description: level=positioning, required. One token or equity id from the entities tool.

from.description: level=calls or episodes. Start of the range, unix seconds, not milliseconds. Required unless you fetch by ids. Episodes match a position open at any point in the range.

to.description: End of the range, unix seconds. Defaults to now.

ids.description: level=calls or episodes. Fetch up to 30 call or episode ids you already hold. No from needed.

handle.description: An X account, with or without @. Telegram channels cannot be filtered on.

entityIds.description: Up to 30 token or equity ids from the entities tool. Matches any of them.

assetClass.description: level=episodes. The market of the position's asset.

limit.description: Items per page, up to 30. Keep it small and page with cursor rather than asking for everything at once.

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous reply. Change any argument but limit and it fails; start again without it.

tools.name: top_accounts
tools.description: X accounts ranked by standing (how much other accounts engage with them) or, with metric, by their track record as callers.. Standing measures attention, not accuracy; track is null for an account that has never opened a position. For the best callers use metric=alphaScore, not avgReturn, which a few big wins or a rally can top. Track metrics rank only accounts with at least 20 scored positions, over every position since late June 2026; quote the number you ranked by with scoredEpisodes. Pass a handle to the calls tool to see its positions.

metric.description: standing (default). alphaScore: return against the market (BTC for crypto, SPY for equities) and outright. hitRate: share of scored positions that made money. avgReturn: mean realized return, not adjusted for the market.

limit.description: Items per page, up to 200. Keep it small and page with cursor rather than asking for everything at once.

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous reply. Change any argument but limit and it fails; start again without it.
